questions.prompt: Explain why, if two similar triangles have sides in the ratio 1 : k, their areas are in the ratio 1 : k².
questions.modelAnswer: Area = ½ × base × height. In the larger triangle, the base is k times as long and the corresponding height is also k times as long (heights are corresponding lengths in similar triangles). So area = ½ × (kb) × (kh) = k² × ½bh. The areas are in the ratio 1 : k².
